text:
andrea: scanning picked up CVE-2026-9999 in our base image (libssl). severity: CRITICAL. do we stop all deploys? also unclear on signer/KMS impact + audit retention needs.

samir: can you paste the image tag and vuln details? need to know if it's in layer we control or upstream distro.

andrea: image: `gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-03-18`
and vuln: `openssl 3.0.6 -> RCE (CVE-2026-9999)` from distro layer. scanner output attached (truncated):
```
VULN: CVE-2026-9999, pkg: openssl, version: 3.0.6, cvss: 9.8
LAYER: /usr/lib/libssl.so.1.1
```

maria: if it's distro-provided layer we still need to rebuild to control runtime surface. important: audit logs for key/sign events will be needed for postmortem. can we extend audit retention for the affected org/window? :eyes:

security-oncall: do NOT rotate/signing keys yet. rotation can break verification if we revoke old versions. short plan: freeze new canaries, produce patched base in staging, run attestations and smoke tests, cosign-sign with existing key version, canary rollout, then rotate keys after all images retired.

leo: question on KMS: we currently use KMS envelope wrapping: `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/image/cryptoKeys/signer-v2`. if we rotate the primary key version, will older signatures still verify?

security-oncall: older signatures remain verifiable as long as the key version used to sign isn't revoked/disabled. verification checks signature against the public key for the version used. so do not disable key versions until we finish cleanup.

devops-bot: image-scan: gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-03-18 -> CVSS 9.8 -> ticket created INC-789 (priority P0).

andrea: propose immediate actions:
- freeze new canaries (no new canary pushes)
- build patched base in staging using distro patch + `strip-debug`
- run full smoke + perf evals (esp. startup/KV cache hit)
- cosign sign & attest using current signer key version
- small canary 2% for 30m, watch errors + latency
- full rollout if green
volunteers for canary watch?

samir: i'll take canary watch. opening RBAC PR to grant the pipeline SA temporary `keystore-signer-role` so the staging builder can sign. MR: `https://gitlab.com/redwood/infra/merge_requests/321` — diff snippet:
```
+ resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "pipeline-keystore" {
+   role = "roles/keystore.signer"
+   members = ["serviceAccount:ci-pipeline@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
+ }
```

maria: we need audit retention extended from 30d -> 180d for the `image-sign` logs and KMS key usage for the org `redwood-prod`. who's owning SIEM/PAL policy change?

security-oncall: assign: owners = ["andrea", "samir"]; sec = "maria"; oncall = "security-oncall". maria - please file the SIEM retention change ticket and tag compliance. i'll coordinate timeline with infra. also open a short timeline doc in /incidents/INC-789.

leo: quick follow-up: if we do the sign with the current key and later rotate, what's our safe revoke policy?

security-oncall: policy: do not disable old key versions for 14 days after last verified production image built; aim for 30 days if possible to cover rollout and rollback windows. communicate in #release-war-room before revocation.

andrea: thanks — i'll start the staging build now and post logs. will ping here when canary is up. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: deploy: staging/base:2026-03-18-patched -> started (build 4521).

maria: filing SIEM ticket now, ETA ~1h for audit retention change PR.

security-oncall: keeping incident channel open. if we see signature verification failures or any `cosign` errors, tag me immediately and escalate to infra oncall.
